ml.title: Understanding ML Performance (in Plain English)
ml.roiExample: Spent $50 on calls → Prevented $350 in lost revenue → ROI = 600%
ml.roiGood: Anything above 300% is excellent ($3 saved per $1 spent)
ml.successRateExample: Made 10 confirmation calls → 7 customers showed up → 70% success
ml.successRateGood: Above 60% means the AI is helping
ml.interventionsSimple: Actions we take to prevent no-shows
ml.interventionsExample: Calling high-risk customers, sending reminders, requiring deposits
ml.interventionsGood: More interventions = better at preventing losses
ml.valueSavedExample: Customer was going to no-show ($250 lost) → We called them → They came → $250 saved
ml.valueSavedGood: Higher is better - means fewer empty tables

pricing.title: Understanding Dynamic Pricing (in Plain English)
pricing.revenueLiftSimple: Extra money from charging more during busy times
pricing.revenueLiftExample: Normal price: $250 → Friday night price: $325 → Revenue lift: $75
pricing.revenueLiftGood: Positive lift = making more money without more customers
pricing.discountsSimple: Money given away to fill empty tables
pricing.discountsGood: OK if it fills tables that would be empty anyway
pricing.netImpactSimple: Revenue lift minus discounts = actual profit
pricing.netImpactExample: Made $5,000 from surges, gave $1,500 in discounts = $3,500 net profit
pricing.netImpactGood: Positive is good! Aim for at least $3 made per $1 given away
pricing.demandExample: Low = lots of empty tables, Surge = fully booked
pricing.demandGood: Surge pricing during high demand, discounts during low

ltv.title: Understanding Customer Value (in Plain English)
ltv.ltvSimple: Total money a customer will spend over time
ltv.ltvExample: Customer visits 4x per year, spends $250 each time, stays 3 years = $3,000 LTV
ltv.ltvGood: Higher LTV = more valuable customer, worth investing in
ltv.frequencyExample: Once a month, twice a year, every week, etc.
ltv.avgSpendSimple: How much they typically spend per visit
ltv.avgSpendExample: Always orders wine and appetizers = higher spend
ltv.retentionExample: Haven't visited in 6 months = high risk of losing them
ltv.retentionGood: Catch at-risk customers early with special offers

dna.title: Understanding Customer DNA (in Plain English)
dna.diningStyleSimple: What type of diner they are
dna.diningStyleExample: Business lunches, romantic dates, family dinners, solo meals
dna.diningStyleGood: Helps you prepare (quiet table for business, kid menu for families)
dna.spontaneityExample: Same-day booker vs plans 2 weeks ahead
dna.spontaneityGood: Planners are reliable, spontaneous need reminders
dna.occasionExample: Birthday, anniversary, business meeting, casual meal
dna.occasionGood: Know what they're celebrating = better service
dna.timePrefExample: Always Friday 8pm, or Tuesday lunch, or weekend brunch
dna.timePrefGood: Predict when they'll book next, send targeted offers

faq.label: FAQ
faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subheading: Everything you need to know about Seatable
faq.ctaSubtext: We're here to help. Reach out to our team anytime.
faq.q1: How does the AI reservation assistant work?
faq.a1: Our AI uses natural language processing to understand customer requests via phone calls or text messages. It checks real-time table availability, handles booking details, and confirms reservations - all without human intervention.
faq.q2: Can I customize the AI's responses?
faq.a2: Yes! Each restaurant can customize the AI's personality, greetings, menu knowledge, and special policies. We train the AI on your specific restaurant details during onboarding.
faq.q3: What happens if the AI can't handle a request?
faq.a3: If the AI encounters a complex situation it can't resolve, it seamlessly transfers the call to your staff with full context of the conversation. This ensures no customer is left frustrated.
faq.a4: Most restaurants are up and running within 24 hours. We'll import your table layout, configure the AI with your menu and policies, and train your staff on the host dashboard.
faq.a5: No special hardware required! Our system works entirely in the cloud. You just need internet access and a device (computer, tablet, or phone) to access the host dashboard.
faq.a6: Absolutely. The AI handles reservation requests, but customers can still speak to staff for special occasions, large parties, or specific questions. The AI and humans work together seamlessly.
faq.q7: What languages does the AI support?
faq.a7: Our AI currently supports 6+ languages including English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian, and German. It auto-detects the caller's language and responds naturally. More languages are being added regularly.
faq.a8: Absolutely. All data is encrypted in transit and at rest. We use enterprise-grade database security with row-level access controls, and we never share your customer data with third parties. You own your data completely.
faq.q9: Can I try it before committing?
faq.a9: Yes! All plans come with a 14-day free trial, no credit card required. You can also try our live AI demo on the website to hear the voice assistant in action before signing up.

host.riskFactorsUnavailable: Detailed risk factors not available for this reservation. Risk score calculated using standard criteria.

riskAction.veryHigh: This reservation has multiple red flags. Require a credit card deposit ({{deposit}}/person) or make a confirmation call to verify they're still coming. Without action, there's a strong chance this party won't show up.
riskAction.high: This reservation shows elevated no-show risk. Call the customer 24 hours before to confirm they're still coming. A quick 2-minute call can prevent an empty table during peak hours.
riskAction.medium: This reservation has some risk factors but nothing alarming. Consider sending an automated reminder a few hours before. No phone call needed unless other concerns arise.
riskAction.low: This reservation looks reliable! The customer has shown commitment signals. No special action needed - just provide excellent service as usual.

riskFactor.newCustomer: No previous visits. First-time guests are statistically more likely to no-show.
riskFactor.highNoShowHistory: This customer has failed to show up for previous reservations.
riskFactor.moderateNoShowHistory: This customer has occasionally missed reservations in the past.
riskFactor.goodHistory: Loyal customer with excellent track record. Very reliable!
riskFactor.veryLargeParty: Large groups ({{threshold}}+) have higher cancellation rates due to coordination challenges.
riskFactor.largeParty: Larger parties are harder to coordinate, increasing no-show risk.
riskFactor.mediumParty: Moderate-sized groups have slightly elevated no-show rates.
riskFactor.sameDayUrgent: Booked very recently - they're coming NOW. Highly committed!
riskFactor.shortNotice: Last-minute bookings (1-2 days) are often impulsive and plans may change.
riskFactor.farAdvance: Booked weeks ahead - plans may change, they may forget, or make other arrangements.
riskFactor.primeTime: Weekend prime-time slots (Fri/Sat 7-9 PM) have highest no-show rates.
riskFactor.peakHour: Popular dinner hours see more no-shows due to high demand and multiple bookings.
riskFactor.noEmail: Phone-only contact makes confirmation harder and suggests less commitment.
riskFactor.tourist: Tourists have higher no-show rates due to travel uncertainties and itinerary changes.
riskFactor.local: Local customers are more reliable and have stronger commitment to showing up.
riskFactor.languageBarrier: Potential communication issues may lead to misunderstandings about reservation.
riskFactor.specialOccasion: Birthday/Anniversary bookings show high commitment - people rarely skip these!
riskFactor.terraceWeatherRisk: Last-minute terrace requests are weather-dependent and may cancel if it rains.
riskFactor.dietaryNeeds: Customers with special dietary needs show intentionality and planning.
riskFactor.firstTimer: First-time visitors are less familiar with the restaurant and slightly less committed.
riskFactor.default: This factor affects the likelihood of the customer showing up.
